title: Replication, Review and Knowledge Freshness
purpose: Seed knowledge-maintenance methodology so Lantern distinguishes replication from repetition, synthesizes bodies of evidence cautiously, and prioritizes review using evidence freshness and domain change rather than naively decaying truth confidence with age.

concepts.definition: A new evidential application testing whether a finding/relation reproduces under specified conditions.
Replication designed to match key original methods/conditions closely enough to test reproducibility.
Replication testing the same underlying claim with meaningfully different operationalizations/methods.
A replication whose result does not reproduce the target effect/prediction to the prespecified evidential standard; interpretation depends on power, fidelity, scope and method.
Ability to obtain consistent computational/analytic results using the same data/code/procedure; distinct from independent replication.
A structured evidence synthesis using explicit search, inclusion, appraisal and synthesis methods.
Quantitative synthesis of effect estimates across studies under a declared statistical model and inclusion criteria.
Distortion when availability/publication of results depends on direction, significance or desirability.
Selective presentation of outcomes/analyses that can distort the apparent evidence base.
Meaningful variation in effects/results across studies, populations, methods or contexts.
Development of improved measurement/design/analysis that can alter how older evidence should be interpreted.
Expected rate at which relevant facts, technology, practice or evidence standards change in a domain.
Most recent time a claim/model was substantively checked against appropriate evidence, not merely accessed/cited.
Priority for re-evaluating knowledge based on importance, uncertainty, domain change, time since meaningful review, contradictions, methodological change and current use.
A maintenance status indicating elevated need for review; it is not a truth value or automatic confidence penalty.
A claim/model has undergone a meaningful review and remains supported within stated scope.
Review supports retaining a claim/model only in a narrower scope.

guards.reason: Citations may repeat/discuss the same evidence without new tests.
Reanalysis can test analytic robustness but is not new independent evidence.
Interpret replication fidelity, uncertainty, power, scope and total evidence before global rejection.
Replication supports the tested scope/method and does not prove universality.
Synthesis quality depends on included studies, bias, heterogeneity, model and methods.
Dependence, bias and weak methods can persist across many studies.
Age alone is not evidence against a claim.
Stale means review is due, not that evidence currently refutes the claim.
Review pressure should trigger investigation rather than mechanical truth decay.
Recency alone does not establish methodological quality or relevance.
Consensus can reduce urgency but does not make knowledge permanently exempt from evidence.
Methodological improvement changes evidential interpretation but older results may remain informative.

invariants: Replication requires a new evidential application; citation, copying and same-data reanalysis are different activities.
Direct and conceptual replication answer related but distinct robustness questions.
Failed replication is evidence to integrate, not an automatic global falsifier.
Systematic reviews/meta-analyses inherit strengths and weaknesses of their search, inclusion, studies and models.
Heterogeneity is information to explain, not merely noise to average away.
Knowledge age alone never determines truth.
Review pressure is separate from truth confidence.
Stale means review due, not false.
Domain change rate affects review urgency: mathematics/formal proofs differ from medicine, cybersecurity or current events.
Methodological improvement can increase review pressure without erasing historical evidence.
Reconfirmation, scope limitation, contestation and supersession preserve belief genealogy.

provenance.authoring_basis: Replication science, systematic evidence synthesis and knowledge-maintenance principles adapted to Lantern's epistemic freshness architecture.
